Activity.description: Something that took place over a period, identified by an IRI so that every piece of evidence it generated names the same activity. Its period is given as dates; prov:startedAtTime and prov:endedAtTime would require timestamps.

endDate.description: Last day of the period, included.

startDate.description: First day of the period, included.

wasAssociatedWith.description: Responsibility of an agent for an activity (PROV), for example the farm operator who carried out the field operations a record documents. Claim-type schemas that describe a domain activity, such as a restoration, name its operator the same way. Use it only on a class that represents an activity (its PROV domain is prov:Activity); such classes declare the ProvActivity mixin. It is not attribution of a Claim: the operator and the claimant may differ, and when they coincide both relations are still stated.

Attestation.description: An issuer's judgment, made at a stated time, about what it targets: exact versions of claims, of other attestations, or a snapshot of claims. As a Claim it is attributed (hasClaimant names the issuer), immutable and revisable with wasRevisionOf; it is about a subject, such as a project or a plot, even when it judges a claim about that subject. It does not carry its own hash or IRI, anchoring state, or a status that changes after it is made: a later judgment is a new Attestation.

appliesRuleSet.description: Identifier of an exact version of a normative rule set applied, such as a credit class, a methodology or a program guide version. It is content and enters the identity of the record. It is distinct from a schema-version declaration, which states which schema the RDF conforms to. Unordered set.

assertedAt.description: When the issuer made the judgment.

description.description: The assertion as the claimant states it in natural language. This is asserted content, not a presentational summary: changing it changes the Claim.

hasClaimant.description: The issuer: the party that makes the judgment and takes responsibility for it.

hasSubject.description: What the judgment is about: a project, plot or other subject. It is stated even when it is also the subject of a targeted claim.

hasTarget.description: What an attestation judges or answers: the identifier of an exact, immutable version of a claim, of another attestation, or of a snapshot (a fixed set of claim versions). Never a logical identifier or label. Unordered set.

outcome.description: The verdict, as a term from the vocabulary of the program or rule set the judgment is made under, for example a registration determination.

rationale.description: Why the issuer reached the outcome.

reliesOn.description: Exact versions of claims or attestations that a judgment depends on without judging them, for example the claim stating an enrolment cutoff that an approval relies on. Each value is the identifier of one immutable version. Specializes dcterms:references, so it asserts neither derivation nor support. Unordered set.

requirement.description: Identifier of a requirement within one version of a rule set or checklist, for example a credit class registration requirement. The identifier must name the checklist version as well as the requirement, because the same short ID can name different requirements in different versions. Unordered set.

scope.description: Where the judgment applies: the subjects it covers, what it explicitly excludes, and what it does not establish.

unbounded.description: True when the issuer explicitly gives the judgment no limits beyond what it targets, so that an unlimited approval is a stated choice rather than an omission. Stated only on an attestation without a scope: the two are exclusive.

url.description: Link to a page with more information about the claim. A pointer for readers, not evidence; cite evidence with hasEvidence.

verificationMethod.description: How the assertion or judgment was established, as structured data, so that a consumer can distinguish, for example, a lab-measured value from a self-attested one. One method per record: its party and date are those of the record that carries it (for an attestation, its issuer and assertedAt), so a subject checked by two methods has two records, each with its own party and date. A value of OTHER must come with verificationMethodDescriptor.

verificationMethodDescriptor.description: Free-text description of a verification method that the VerificationMethodType enumeration does not cover; required when verificationMethod is OTHER. It is the extension path: a method that recurs is added to the enumeration in a later schema version.

wasRevisionOf.description: Identifier of the exact, immutable earlier Claim version that this Claim revises, typically its ClaimIRI. A Claim has no identifier slot, because its ClaimIRI is computed over its canonical form outside Claim content (regen-network/claims#1), so the value is a bare IRI and the slot names no class. It never names a logical claim or version family. In PROV a revision implies that both versions are aspects of the same thing (alternateOf), so use it only for a revised version of the same assertion; a separate, later assertion, such as a follow-up observation, is a new Claim and is not a revision. The earlier version is unchanged, its attestations do not carry over, and selecting a current version happens outside the Claim.

assertedAt.description: When the claimants made this assertion. hasClaimant.description: The agent or agents that take responsibility for making this assertion: an individual, organization or community. A collective that asserts as one body is a single claimant of type COMMUNITY or ORGANIZATION; listing it does not make its members co-claimants. Specializes prov:wasAttributedTo, so under PROV each claimant is an agent associated with the activity that generated the Claim, which is the act of asserting. Unordered set.

hasEvidence.description: Sources the claimant presents as evidence for the assertion, each an Evidence node identified by the IRI of the exact version cited. Whether a source actually supports the assertion is judged separately, by attestations. Specializes dcterms:references. Unordered set.

hasSubject.description: What the claim is about, as a ClaimSubject node identified by its IRI: a place, plot, project, organization, community, indicator, dataset or another claim. Claims about the same subject share its IRI and can be joined. Specialized claim schemas narrow the range to a subclass of ClaimSubject. Not the claimant, and not necessarily the feature of interest of an observation inside the claim.

url.description: Link to a page with more information about the claim. A pointer for readers, not evidence; cite evidence with hasEvidence.

wasRevisionOf.description: Identifier of the exact, immutable earlier Claim version that this Claim revises, typically its ClaimIRI. A Claim has no identifier slot, because its ClaimIRI is computed over its canonical form outside Claim content (regen-network/claims#1), so the value is a bare IRI and the slot names no class. It never names a logical claim or version family. In PROV a revision implies that both versions are aspects of the same thing (alternateOf), so use it only for a revised version of the same assertion; a separate, later assertion, such as a follow-up observation, is a new Claim and is not a revision. The earlier version is unchanged, its attestations do not carry over, and selecting a current version happens outside the Claim.

RegistryFindingAttestation.description: A finding raised in a Regen Registry review: a corrective action, clarification or forward action request, or a material issue raised by the Registry Agent. A finding states its type and cites at least one piece of evidence. Later assessments of the finding and replies to it are RegistryReviewAttestations that target it and carry the same findingLabel.

appliesRuleSet.description: Identifier of an exact version of a normative rule set applied, such as a credit class, a methodology or a program guide version. It is content and enters the identity of the record. It is distinct from a schema-version declaration, which states which schema the RDF conforms to. Unordered set.

assertedAt.description: When the issuer made the judgment.

conditions.description: Obligations the judgment carries to a later milestone, such as follow-up actions due before verification. Unordered set.

description.description: The assertion as the claimant states it in natural language. This is asserted content, not a presentational summary: changing it changes the Claim.

findingLabel.description: The issuer's own identifier for a finding, stable across review rounds, such as "CL 07(1)". It groups the dated records about one finding; it is not the identifier of any of them.

hasClaimant.description: The issuer: the party that makes the judgment and takes responsibility for it.

hasSubject.description: What the judgment is about: a project, plot or other subject. It is stated even when it is also the subject of a targeted claim.

hasTarget.description: What an attestation judges or answers: the identifier of an exact, immutable version of a claim, of another attestation, or of a snapshot (a fixed set of claim versions). Never a logical identifier or label. Unordered set.

issuerRole.description: The capacity in which the issuer acts, so that a consumer can check the issuer's authority for the decision.

outcome.description: The verdict, as the IRI of a RegistryReviewOutcome term, for example rfs:ApprovedForRegistration. Required: a registry review is recorded when there is a judgment, and each dated record states its verdict or the finding's status as of its date. A requirement that cannot yet be decided is rfs:RequirementPending, not an omitted outcome.

rationale.description: Why the issuer reached the outcome.

reliesOn.description: Exact versions of claims or attestations that a judgment depends on without judging them, for example the claim stating an enrolment cutoff that an approval relies on. Each value is the identifier of one immutable version. Specializes dcterms:references, so it asserts neither derivation nor support. Unordered set.

requirement.description: Identifier of a requirement within one version of a rule set or checklist, for example a credit class registration requirement. The identifier must name the checklist version as well as the requirement, because the same short ID can name different requirements in different versions. Unordered set.

scope.description: Where the judgment applies: the subjects it covers, what it explicitly excludes, and what it does not establish.

unbounded.description: True when the issuer explicitly gives the judgment no limits beyond what it targets, so that an unlimited approval is a stated choice rather than an omission. Stated only on an attestation without a scope: the two are exclusive.

url.description: Link to a page with more information about the claim. A pointer for readers, not evidence; cite evidence with hasEvidence.

verificationMethod.description: How the assertion or judgment was established, as structured data, so that a consumer can distinguish, for example, a lab-measured value from a self-attested one. One method per record: its party and date are those of the record that carries it (for an attestation, its issuer and assertedAt), so a subject checked by two methods has two records, each with its own party and date. A value of OTHER must come with verificationMethodDescriptor.

verificationMethodDescriptor.description: Free-text description of a verification method that the VerificationMethodType enumeration does not cover; required when verificationMethod is OTHER. It is the extension path: a method that recurs is added to the enumeration in a later schema version.

wasRevisionOf.description: Identifier of the exact, immutable earlier Claim version that this Claim revises, typically its ClaimIRI. A Claim has no identifier slot, because its ClaimIRI is computed over its canonical form outside Claim content (regen-network/claims#1), so the value is a bare IRI and the slot names no class. It never names a logical claim or version family. In PROV a revision implies that both versions are aspects of the same thing (alternateOf), so use it only for a revised version of the same assertion; a separate, later assertion, such as a follow-up observation, is a new Claim and is not a revision. The earlier version is unchanged, its attestations do not carry over, and selecting a current version happens outside the Claim.

RegistryReviewOutcome.description: Outcomes of Regen Registry review judgments, used as outcome values by their meaning IRIs (for example rfs:ApprovedForRegistration).
